note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Token-pruning safety evaluation, attention-collapse mechanism, SAP defense and its validation

nodes.name: Token pruning raises jailbreak vulnerability
nodes.description: Most token-pruning strategies (vision-centric and text-guided) raise average ASR over the unpruned LLaVA-1.5-7B (54.01%), e.g. TRIM 62.33%, FitPrune 63.14%, SparseVLM 62.73%, with text-guided pruning the worst.

nodes.name: Degradation is not capacity loss
nodes.description: As pruning ratio rises from 0% to 80%, ASR rises substantially while utility stays stable, and random pruning keeps ASR stable (52.73%), so safety loss stems from biased token selection rather than token reduction.

nodes.name: Query-based compression improves safety
nodes.description: Query-based compression (LLaVA-Mini, LLaVA-MQT) reduces ASR (LLaVA-Mini 31.98% vs 54.01% baseline) even at 99.3-99.8% compression, so safety need not trade off against acceleration.

nodes.name: Pruning-Induced Malicious Amplification
nodes.description: Pruning removes background tokens that act as a benign semantic buffer, forcing attention to collapse onto a few retained foreground tokens carrying malicious semantics, which then dominate generation under jailbreak prompts.

nodes.name: Attention visualization contrast
nodes.description: TRIM concentrates attention on a few foreground tokens whereas LLaVA-Mini keeps attention balanced across the whole image.

nodes.name: Temperature intervention
nodes.description: Sharpening TRIM's image-token attention by lowering temperature from 1.9 to 1.0 reduces attention entropy from 2.8 to 2.3 and raises ASR from 58% to 65% while SQA accuracy stays stable, linking attention collapse to vulnerability.

nodes.name: Malicious semantic density theory
nodes.description: With malicious energy S and safety buffer energy N, density rho = S/(S+N); pruning drives N toward 0 so rho approaches 1 even if S is unchanged, while random pruning keeps E[rho] approximately unchanged.

nodes.name: SAP three-stage defense
nodes.description: Safety-Aware Pruning is training-free and inference-time with three steps: Malicious Anchor Identification, Benign Token Restoration and Attention Reallocation.

nodes.name: Malicious anchor score
nodes.description: Malicious anchors are the top-m retained visual tokens ranked by MSA score, the product of text-to-visual attention and cosine deviation from a precomputed safety-aligned semantic vector.

nodes.name: Benign token restoration
nodes.description: BTR uniformly samples k pruned background tokens and swaps them for the k lowest-importance retained tokens, keeping sequence length unchanged.

nodes.name: Attention reallocation
nodes.description: AR scales malicious-anchor attention by (1 - lambda) and redistributes the removed mass uniformly to the restored benign tokens, requiring no softmax recomputation.

nodes.name: SAP main safety results
nodes.description: Across five pruning methods SAP reduces average ASR by 18.8-27.6% (relative), e.g. PruMerge 61.88 to 44.78, with utility changes within about 2%.

nodes.name: BTR and AR are complementary
nodes.description: On TRIM, BTR alone gives modest ASR gains (MM-Safety 65.87 to 63.89), AR alone lowers it to 53.57 but cuts MMBench from 66.92 to 63.23, and combining both gives 52.78 with MMBench 67.27.

nodes.name: SAP is efficient
nodes.description: SAP adds negligible cost over TRIM: latency 57.19 ms vs 55.90 ms, memory 14.53 GB, identical 2.22T FLOPs, versus 94.29 ms for the original model.

nodes.name: SAP restores attention entropy
nodes.description: With TRIM+SAP, attention entropy is restored toward the original model's pattern, mitigating attention collapse.

nodes.name: Textual extension
nodes.description: Applying MAI, BTR and AR to textual tokens (SAP-dagger) reduces FasterVLM MM-Safety ASR by 62% (72.02 to 10.32), showing the principle is modality-agnostic.

isolated_nodes.name: Guardrail comparison
isolated_nodes.description: SAP achieves safety comparable to LLaVAGuard on TRIM (MM-Safety 52.78 vs 51.59) at much lower latency (57.19 ms vs 160.09 ms).

isolated_nodes.name: Optimal anchor count
isolated_nodes.description: m=10 malicious anchors is optimal on TRIM: FigStep ASR drops from 62.20 to 47.80 with MMBench 67.27, while m=30 drops MMBench to 59.02 with no safety gain.

isolated_nodes.name: Robust across pruning ratios
isolated_nodes.description: From 50% to 90% pruning SAP keeps ASR low on MM-Safety and FigStep and SQA utility stable.

isolated_nodes.name: Pruning paradigms
isolated_nodes.description: Token pruning methods fall into vision-centric selection, text-guided selection and query-based compression.

structural_reasoning: Argument runs from empirical safety findings, to the attention-collapse mechanism with supporting interventions and theory, to the SAP design and its validation.
